Hi, I've been looking trying to formalize some GR and yesterday someone brought my attention to #36845. The issue is that this PR (together with a lot of the existing mathlib4 code) only applies for Riemannian manifolds rather than the psuedo-Riemannian manifolds of GR. As far as I can tell, the reason for imposing the stronger condition that the metric is positive definite rather than merely non-degenerate is so that the metric can induce a topology on fibers. The following quote is from Topology/VectorBundle/Riemannian.lean:

If one wants to endow an existing vector bundle with a Riemannian metric, there is a subtlety:
the inner product space structure on the fibers should give rise to a topology on the fibers
which is defeq to the original one, to avoid diamonds. To do this, we introduce a
class [RiemannianBundle E] containing the data of an inner
product on the fibers defining the same topology as the original one. Given this class, we can
construct NormedAddCommGroup and InnerProductSpace instances on the fibers, compatible in a
defeq way with the initial topology. If the data used to register the instance RiemannianBundle E
depends continuously on the base point, we register automatically an instance of
[IsContinuousRiemannianBundle F E] (and similarly if the data is smooth).

Is it the case that if I want to construct Levi-Civita connections on psuedo-Riemannian manifolds, there is a lot of infrastructure I have to build from scratch? Or is there a simple way to weaken the positivity assumption on the metric to non-degeneracy in a way that doesn't break the entire dependency chain?

@Michael Kiss If it can help there is a WIP implementation of PseudoRiemannianMetric (only one of the several possible options) in physlib #968 which aims to complement the recent mathlib RiemannanBundle and Levi-Civita pipeline and where any review or contribution is more than welcome.

Great I'll check that out, thanks! I don't know much about physlean (or just lean in general lol), but has there been much progress towards formalizing gauge theory? In particular things like principal bundles, associated vector bundles, principal Ehresmann connections etc?

A good way to be up to date with what is going on is to search and navigate mathlib/physlib open (and closed) PR s and make use of the zulip search bar as there has been several posts related to what you are interested in, like
#new members > Looking for Differential Geometry Project
